sec-head.p: What I build to clarify when semantic, keyword, or hybrid search fits your retrieval needs.

card.p: An independent audit of your search requirements and data characteristics, resulting in a written recommendation: semantic, keyword, hybrid, or a custom combination with benchmarks.
Embedding-based retrieval with vector databases: dense passage indexing, approximate nearest neighbor search, and relevance scoring for understanding user intent beyond exact matches.
BM25 and inverted index implementations: tokenization, stemming, stop-word handling, and ranked retrieval for precise term-matching scenarios like legal or technical documentation.
Reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) or weighted blending of semantic and keyword results, balancing intent understanding with exact-match precision, configurable per query type.
Systematic diagnosis of search failures: identifying when semantic search misses critical keywords or keyword search misses synonyms, then building hybrid mitigations.

card cta-card.p: Run the quick fit-check above, or let's scope it properly.

ul: User queries use synonyms, paraphrases, or natural language: semantic search captures meaning with 15-30% better recall than keyword-only approaches
High query variability: embedding similarity handles diverse phrasings without manual synonym expansion
Sparse keyword matches lead to zero results: semantic search retrieves relevant documents even when no exact terms align
You need to surface conceptually related content, not just literal matches, for discovery or recommendation use cases
Searching for unique identifiers, codes, or proper nouns: BM25 achieves near-perfect precision for specific terms like part numbers or legal citations
Domain-specific jargon or rare terms: keyword search directly matches without embedding noise or dilution from vector similarity
Low-latency requirements: inverted index lookups are 2-5x faster than embedding generation + ANN search
Hybrid search is essential when both fail: RRF blending yields 20-30% higher NDCG@10 on diverse query sets compared to either method alone
